elements.element: Fallback: licence/access and use rights extend to Customer's affiliates
elements.evidence: "extend to any affiliate of the Company"

elements.element: Fallback: affiliate coverage conditioned on written notice to Vendor
Fallback: rights transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction
elements.evidence: "may be transferred to a successor to the Company's business in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Preferred: licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf
elements.evidence: Insertion names only "any affiliate of the Company"; no contractor language anywhere.

elements.element: Preferred: affiliates covered without a notice condition
elements.evidence: "covered by written notice to HDI" imposes the fallback condition.

elements.element: Preferred: paid-up licences perpetual and irrevocable
elements.evidence: No perpetuity/irrevocability language in clause 1.4 or the insertion.

elements.element: Preferred: subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach

elements.evidence: Transfer limited to "a successor ... in a merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of its assets".

reasons: The single inserted sentence completes both fallback atomic elements: affiliate extension on written notice and transfer to an M&A successor.
No preferred-only scope (contractors) or duration (perpetual/irrevocable, breach-only termination) was added, so the locked fallback level is hit cleanly.
Minimality holds: one concise sentence appended to an otherwise untouched Section 1.4, with no rewrite of the bandwidth, hosting or administration-tool commitments.
Intent preserved: no undefined terms, contradictions or dangling mechanics; "affiliate" and the M&A trigger are self-contained and Company/HDI are defined parties.
